alt: A ladder of five sizes running from the 0.1 mm limit of unaided vision down to the 2 nm width of the DNA double helix, with a colonic crypt, one crypt cell, and the light-microscope limit in between.
longDescription: Five rungs, largest at the top. Rung one: the finest detail the unaided eye separates, about 0.1 mm, which is 100 micrometres. Rung two: one colonic crypt, a tube of roughly 700 cells stacked about 32 along its length, so its length is a few hundred micrometres. Rung three: one colonic epithelial cell, about 10 to 20 micrometres across. Rung four: the finest detail a conventional light microscope separates, about 0.25 micrometres, which is 250 nanometres. Rung five: the DNA double helix, about 2 nanometres across. The steps between rungs are, in order: the crypt is roughly three to six times larger than the eye's threshold, so a crypt opening is at the edge of what an unaided eye could resolve; one crypt cell is about thirty times shorter than the whole crypt; a crypt cell is about forty to eighty times wider than the light microscope's limit, so a lens shows the cell easily; and the light-microscope limit is about a hundred times wider than the DNA helix, so no light microscope shows the helix at all. A separate step runs directly from the eye's threshold to the cell and carries the lesson's central ratio: a cell is five to ten times smaller than the finest detail the unaided eye resolves, which is the gap a lens had to close before anyone could see that tissue is built from cells.
